stage1_evidence_shown.label: BACKGROUND
stage1_evidence_shown.context: Physical examination to detect abdominal injuries has been considered unreliable in alcohol-intoxicated trauma patients. Computed tomography (CT) plays the primary role in these abdominal evaluations.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: METHODS
stage1_evidence_shown.context: We reviewed medical records of all blunt trauma patients admitted to our trauma service from January 1, 1992, to March 31, 1998. Study patients had a blood alcohol level>or =80 mg/dL, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 15, and unremarkable abdominal examination.

stage1_model_output.raw: {"action":"ANSWER","answer":"maybe","confidence":0.35,"reason_for_action":"Background states exam is unreliable in intoxicated patients and CT is primary, but provided methods give no outcome data—insufficient evidence to conclude CT is always necessary."}

stage2_added_evidence.label: RESULTS
stage2_added_evidence.context: Of 324 patients studied, 317 (98%) had CT scans negative for abdominal injury. Abdominal injuries were identified in 7 patients (2%), with only 2 (0.6%) requiring abdominal exploration. A significant association was found between major chest injury and abdominal injury.
